# #749 — dream.light and dream.rem have never run: registered as handlers, enqueued by nothing, so candidates never promote to thoughts/decisions

## What

`dream.light` and `dream.rem` handlers are registered in
`composeMaintenanceHandlers` but **have never executed once**. Verified against
the dogfood database 2026-08-25:

```
job_kind       | state     | count | max(created_at)
memory.distill | succeeded |   398 | 2026-08-25 08:06:51
memory.distill | queued    |     1 | 2026-08-25 08:07:27
system.facts   | succeeded |    30 | 2026-07-26 23:40:28
```

No `dream.light` row. No `dream.rem` row. Ever.

The reason is documented in the code itself
(`src/maintenance-bootstrap.ts:189-191`):

> NONE OF THESE ENQUEUE ANYTHING. Registration is dispatch only. The recurring
> producer starts below after this map and the durable queue exist; manual
> DREAM cycles remain available through `scripts/dream-cycle.ts`.

`runMaintenanceSweep` enqueues `memory.distill` and `graph.derive` only --
confirmed, no `dream` reference in `src/maintenance-sweep.ts`. So Light and REM
run only when someone invokes `scripts/dream-cycle.ts` or
`scripts/dream-light-run.ts` by hand. Nobody has since 2026-08-08.

## Consequence

The distill pipeline was repaired today (#747, four stacked defects) and is now
draining: `candidate_memory` is filling in real time.

```
candidate_memory  13,434   newest row 2026-08-25   <- filling now
thoughts          26,453   newest row 2026-08-08   <- frozen
decisions         18,048   newest row 2026-08-08   <- frozen
```

`thoughts` and `decisions` are what recall reads. Candidates accumulate and
nothing promotes them, so repairing distill does not by itself restore recall
-- it moves the stall one stage later. Anything captured since 2026-08-08 is
extracted but not yet reachable.

## The question this issue holds

Whether Light/REM should have an autonomous producer is a **product decision**,
not a defect to patch. `docs/dream-design.md` owns triggers, budgets, and
autonomy, and the bootstrap comment reads as a deliberate choice to keep DREAM
manual rather than an oversight.

Options, without a recommendation because the call is the operator's:

1. **Recurring producer in the sweep**, matching how `memory.distill` and
   `graph.derive` are scheduled. Consistent with the existing shape; makes
   promotion continuous.
2. **Scheduled cycle** (launchd/cron invoking `scripts/dream-cycle.ts`) so
   DREAM stays a distinct phase with its own cadence rather than a per-tick
   job.
3. **Stay manual**, and the gap is documentation plus an operator runbook step
   rather than code.

Whichever is chosen, the current state is worth naming: promotion has no
automatic path at all, and that was invisible because the tables it feeds still
held data from before it stopped.

## Discussion (1)

### rodaddy — 2026-08-25T12:19:32Z

## Correction from the operator: this is not a wiring gap

I filed this as "handlers registered, enqueued by nothing." That framing was
wrong, and the operator corrected it: the stages that would promote are not
coded to do the promoting yet. Verified against source before re-filing.

**`dream.light` (`src/dream-light.ts`, 534 lines) does not promote.** It writes
`content_occurrences` and stamps `light_swept_at` on `ob_raw_turns`. No insert
into `thoughts` or `decisions`.

**`dream.rem` (`src/dream-rem.ts`, 704 lines) does not promote either, by
design.** `rg 'INSERT INTO' src/dream-rem.ts` returns nothing. Its own header
says so:

> REM IS A PREP STAGE, NOT A JUDGE (docs/dream-design.md:274-280): it finds,
> groups, and packages work so Deep does not have to go looking [...]
> THE ONE HARD RULE. REM MAY write machine_grade + machine_grade_model. It MUST
> NEVER write review_action, reviewed_at, or graded_by.

`docs/dream-design.md:128` states the split directly: **"REM prepares, Deep
commits."** Deep is #394/#396, runs off-box, and is not built. `dream-design.md:44`
already tracks the consequence as a known-true gap: `graduateLaneEvent` has
never written a row, `thoughts WHERE promoted_from ? 'graduated_at'` is 0.

So there is no scheduling decision to make here. Enqueuing Light and REM on a
cadence would not move a single row into `thoughts` or `decisions`, because
neither stage writes there. The missing piece is Deep, and the operator
confirms that work is already mapped in an existing sprint rather than being
new.

## What remains true and worth keeping

The measurement stands, and it is the useful part of this issue:

```
candidate_memory  26,896   newest row 2026-08-25   <- filling now
thoughts          26,453   newest row 2026-08-08   <- frozen
decisions         18,048   newest row 2026-08-08   <- frozen
```

Also verified: `dream.light` and `dream.rem` have zero rows in
`maintenance_jobs`, ever.

The distill repair in #747 is real and is draining (8,028 -> 43,919 turns
distilled as of writing, candidates rising with it). What that fix does NOT do
is restore recall, because the stage that would carry candidates into the
tables recall reads does not exist yet. Worth stating plainly so #747 closing
is not mistaken for "memory works again."

## Disposition

Closing as **not a defect** — the behaviour is the designed one, and the real
work (Deep) is tracked in the existing sprint. Reopening would be right only
if someone concludes Light/REM should be scheduled for their OWN sake
(tiering, machine grading) independent of promotion, which is a separate
question this issue did not ask.

cc #747 for the pipeline context.
